title: Sorting and Counting
short: Sort objects into groups, count each group and order them.

blocks.html: Sorting means putting things that are alike together. Then you can count each group and compare them.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: A jumble of apples, stars and balls. Tap one kind at a time to count it.

items: Choose a sorting rule: by kind, color or size.
Put each thing in its group.
Put the groups in order from fewest to most.

blocks.html: Sort by a rule, count each group, then compare the numbers.
Sorting turns a jumble into groups. Groups are easy to count and compare.

blocks.title: Which has the most?
blocks.q: Sort the picture above. Which kind has the most?
steps: Stars have the most. Balls have the fewest.

blocks.html: For grown-ups: Sort laundry, toys or snacks together. Ask, “Which group has the most? Which has the fewest?”

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.MD.B.3: classify objects into categories, count each category and sort the categories by count
Institute of Education Sciences practice guide: Teaching Math to Young Children (NCEE 2014-4005)
